prompt: Users of loyalty-agent/ are identified by their loyalty card number: 8 digits, handed out in sequence. Anyone who holds our traces or logs must not be able to tell which card a conversation belongs to by hashing card numbers. Staging and production are deployed; I keep the secret values in .env.staging and .env.prod and run all cluster commands myself.

checks.why: PRINCIPAL_HASH_SALT is a secret: only the manifest's secrets.keys reach the app Secret

checks.expr: all(k in get(data, 'secrets.keys', []) for k in ('OPENAI_API_KEY', 'JUDGE_API_KEY', 'POSTGRES_DSN', 'LANGSMITH_API_KEY'))

checks.why: secrets never go into chart values
a configuration-only change: the app already reads this setting
the value reaches the cluster only through `graph-agents-cli secrets apply --env <env>`
pods read a changed Secret only when they start: `deploy --restart --env <env>`

reference: The hashed principal id is plain sha256 unless PRINCIPAL_HASH_SALT is set (then HMAC-keyed), and sequential card numbers are trivially guessable. The app already reads the salt: the change is configuration only. Add PRINCIPAL_HASH_SALT to `secrets.keys` in the manifest (never to values files, never in code), and tell the user to put a long random value in .env.staging and .env.prod, run `graph-agents-cli secrets apply --env staging` / `--env prod`, then `graph-agents-cli deploy --restart --env <env>` (a Secret change alone does not restart pods). Changing the salt changes every hash.
